Interpretation: Sinus bradycardia with 1st degree AV block. Causes: Athletes, beta-blockers, digoxin, hypothyroidism, inferior MI. Management: If asymptomatic + haemodynamically stable → observe. agent_evaluations.detailed_feedback: This OSCE collection FAILS radiology interpretation standards due to critical deficiencies in clinical content depth. While the metadata structure and Australian reference sources are strong, ALL 52 OSCEs lack the fundamental requirement for radiology interpretation exercises: systematic image interpretation using established frameworks (ABCDE for CXR, 7-step for ECG, ABC for CT). The scenarios are generic task descriptions ('Assess and manage X') without actual imaging findings, systematic analysis, differential diagnoses, or clinical correlation. Placeholder image file paths point to non-existent files, making these OSCEs non-executable as written. For AMC Clinical Examination preparation, radiology interpretation stations require students to demonstrate systematic approaches, identify critical findings using Australian terminology, correlate imaging with clinical presentation, and propose evidence-based management. None of this is present. MANDATORY REVISION REQUIRED: Add complete systematic interpretations with specific imaging findings, model answers, marking rubrics aligned to AMC 70% pass standard, and Australian radiological terminology (RANZCR standards). Current state: 17/52 OSCEs are mislabeled (laboratory tests, not imaging), 35/52 imaging OSCEs lack interpretable content. Estimated revision time: 40-60 hours to bring to AMC Clinical Examination readiness standard. Recommend prioritizing high-yield topics first: ECG interpretation (OSCEs 9, 12, 13, 19 - STEMI recognition is AMC core competency), CXR interpretation (OSCEs 18, 27, 28 - pneumonia, pulmonary edema, lung cancer), CT head (OSCE 49 - stroke, most time-critical). This collection has strong foundational structure but requires substantial clinical content development before deployment for AMC candidate preparation.
